narrative.summary: Kazakhstan regulates AI through a dedicated, risk-based Law on Artificial Intelligence signed in November 2025 and in force since early 2026, with a companion law adding automated-decision rights to the personal data law and a growing set of implementing orders from the new Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development (criteria for AI systems, high-risk lists, documentation, access to computing and the national AI platform). The 2026 Digital Code covers algorithmic systems and a constitutional law on Alatau City allows AI experimental legal regimes. Policy follows the AI Development Concept 2024-2029 and the 2026 Digital Qazaqstan strategy, with a presidential AI Development Council, an AI standard for secondary schools and a national AI standard.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft-acts portal and the presidential and parliament websites could not be reached, so some recent decrees and drafts are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Закон Республики Казахстан от 17 ноября 2025 года № 230-VIII «Об искусственном интеллекте»
instruments.english_title: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of Kazakhstan (signed by the President)
instruments.current_status: Signed 17 November 2025 and published in Egemen Qazaqstan and Kazakhstanskaya Pravda No. 222 on 18 November 2025 (Adilet register No. 217048). Art. 31: enters into force sixty calendar days after first official publication. Amended by Law No. 326-VIII of 24 June 2026 (arts 1, 13, 17, 20, 28); Adilet lists the act as amended to 25 August 2026. An unofficial English translation is listed on Adilet. Implementing orders adopted in 2026 are recorded separately.
instruments.summary: Kazakhstan's framework AI law. It sets regulatory principles (legality, fairness, transparency and explainability, accountability, human well-being, data protection, safety), the competences of the Government and the authorised AI body, classifies AI systems by risk (minimal, medium, high) and by autonomy, and bans systems that manipulate behaviour, exploit vulnerabilities, perform social scoring, infer sensitive traits from biometrics or recognise emotions without consent. Owners and operators must manage risks across the life cycle (reviewed at least annually), users must be told when goods or services are produced with AI, synthetic AI outputs must carry machine-readable and visible labels, and the law also covers trusted lists of high-risk systems, AI audits, copyright, liability for harm, the national AI platform and data libraries.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main AI statute; legal basis for the Ministry's implementing orders.

instruments.summary: Companion law to the AI Law that aligns other statutes with it. Among other changes it inserts Article 19-1 into the Law on Personal Data and their Protection, which bans automated processing of personal data that creates, changes or ends a person's rights unless the person consents or a law allows it, and requires controllers to explain automated processing, accept objections and answer them within three working days.

instruments.summary: Codified law on the digital environment, digital objects and state digitalisation. Article 43 defines algorithmic systems (including AI systems), prohibits discriminatory algorithmic decisions and gives people subject to fully automated decisions the right to be told an algorithmic system was used, to an explanation of the key factors, and to a human review where the decision has legal effects. Article 100 provides that quality audits of AI systems assess the quality and lawfulness of the data libraries used for training.

instruments.summary: AFSA report on its 2025 survey of all AIFC Authorised Persons (42 responses): 45% use AI, mostly in lower-risk areas such as customer communication and marketing, with heavy reliance on third-party tools and few full-scale deployments. AFSA states it will run another survey in 2026 to decide whether regulatory amendments on AI in financial services are needed, and invites firms to test AI solutions in the AIFC FinTech Lab sandbox.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. New adilet.zan.kz front end JavaScript-only and its API needs a login (laws read on the official old.adilet.zan.kz edition; source_url old.adilet, official_webpage_url new adilet). legalacts.egov.kz JavaScript-only; parlam.kz and akorda.kz no connection; zan.gov.kz TLS failure. ~1,600 gov.kz document titles of the AI ministry scanned via its public content API. AI Law and Digital Code effective dates not printed. Kazakhstan is not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Adilet (Ministry of Justice legal information system) searched through its server-rendered edition (full-text 'искусственного интеллекта', 1,651 hits; first 60 reviewed; 'Цифровой кодекс'). Recorded: AI Law 230-VIII, companion law 231-VIII, Personal Data Law (Art. 19-1 automated decisions), Digital Code 255-VIII (Art. 43 algorithmic systems), Alatau City constitutional law (Art. 54 AI experimental regimes). The new Constitution (referendum 15 March 2026) has no AI provision. No pending AI bill found; legalacts.egov.kz (draft acts portal) not searched (JavaScript-only).; Government: Presidential decrees (AI Development Council 2025; Digital Qazaqstan strategy 2026), Government resolutions (AI Concept 2024-2029; national AI platform operator; Digital Qazaqstan action plan) recorded. Year of Digitalisation and AI 2026 decree and the commission for it seen, not recorded (no AI governance content). No national AI procurement rules or AI ethics code found.; Ministries: Ministry of AI and Digital Development: all ~1,600 document records on gov.kz scanned by title; AI Law implementing orders recorded (criteria, documentation list, trusted high-risk lists, machine-readable forms, platform interaction, computing access, Alem GPT pilot). Ministry of Enlightenment AI standard for schools recorded. Other ministries (health, justice, defence, finance, labour, interior) only covered via Adilet full-text search; nothing AI-specific beyond professional standards and pilot automation orders.; Regulators: Personal-data protection is administered by the Ministry (no separate DPA guidance on AI found; its 2025-2026 personal-data security recommendations are generic). Gosstandart: ST RK ISO/IEC 5339-2025 recorded. AFSA (AIFC): generative AI survey report recorded; no AI rules. National Bank: regulatory sandbox exists but is not AI-specific; no AI guidance found. Information security committee: no AI-specific guidance found. Convention 108: no ratification or accession act found in an Adilet full-text search (convention108 set to null).. Not reached: legalacts.egov.kz draft acts portal (JavaScript-only) - drafts and consultations not checked there; parlam.kz (Mazhilis/Senate) - not reachable by curl from this environment; Ministry-by-ministry gov.kz document scans other than the Ministry of AI and Digital Development; Kazakh-language queries beyond Adilet's bilingual records. Could not verify: The new adilet.zan.kz front end and its API (auth required) could not be read; all law texts were read on old.adilet.zan.kz, the same Ministry of Justice system; zan.gov.kz (Reference Control Bank) failed TLS verification; akorda.kz and parlam.kz not reachable by curl. procurement, cyber-security, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
